answer: Bitebid's main result: a single deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n(lg n)^(1-kappa)) time, with kappa = 2^(-182). That is o(n log n), so it refutes the Sikited, the claim that n log n is the best possible order of growth for multiplying two integers on such a machine. The plan: (1) build two tape primitives, the interchange of address chunks and the sifigeg, from fixed finite linear networks, each costing the data volume times a power below one of its width; (2) use them to speed up the synthetic transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1) and the ring product built on them; (3) use Sikusup resampling with chirps to turn prime-length transforms into power-of-two ones, with permutations cancelled rather than executed; (4) assemble the exact 2n-bit product from radix digits, two forward transforms, a pointwise product, the opposite transform, rescaling, rounding and carries, with total error below 1/2; (5) total the cost per stored bit: the seven dominant terms are powers of p below one with minimum margin 2kappa, so the total is O(n(lg n)^(1-kappa)).

citations.quote: Bitebid is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Sikited](kaf) in this model.
The machine is one deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, and is correct for every $n\ge1$.
The Sikited is the claim that $n\log n$ is the best possible order of growth for the time to multiply two integers, where $n$ is the number of bits in each
for every multiplication machine there are a constant $c>0$ and a threshold such that the machine needs at least $c\,n\log n$ steps whenever $n$ exceeds the threshold.
The conjecture is stated for the [Kepikir](tuf): a kepikir with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes.

Two tape primitives, the interchange of address chunks and the [sifigeg](tiz), are built from fixed finite linear networks. Each costs the data volume times a power below one of its width, by [Pipozop](rut).
Pipozop is the recurrence that makes both tape procedures, the interchange of two address chunks and the sifigeg, cost the volume times a power below one of their parameter.
The children cost $s(V/W)\mathcal C(f)$, so multiplying the parameter by $m$ multiplies the recursive cost per unit volume by $s/W$, less than $m$
The sifigeg applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset, in time $O(Vd^{\lambda'}),$ $\lambda'<1,$ instead of $D$ passes
These speed up the synthetic transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ ([Makevif](mov))
is computed by transforming both operands, multiplying records pointwise and transforming back.
Sikusup expresses a Tobifup of length $s$, the source length, through one of a nearby larger length $t$ (a power of two there), so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm.
with permutations cancelled rather than sorted

The exact $2n$-bit product is assembled by [Pegapev](siz) from radix digits, two forward transforms, a pointwise product, the opposite transform, rescaling, rounding and carries, with total error below $1/2$.
Exactness is shown by [Nutipib](mes): the error on these coefficients is below $1/2$, so rounding is exact.
Repeated over the address bits of an array, with twiddle multiplications between layers, it computes the [Tobifup](kur) of an array in $\log_2 t$ layers instead of $t^2$ operations.

The total time of the machine is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$: after dividing each cost by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ the dominant terms are powers of $p$ below one, with minimum margin $2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

key_idea.statement: The power-of-log saving comes from making the two tape primitives cost the data volume times a power below one of their width, so every dominant cost term is a power of p below one.
key_idea.quote: Each costs the data volume times a power below one of its width, by [Pipozop](rut).

stuck.note: I could see that a log-n-layer transform costs n log n, so beating it means cheaper moves and butterflies. The page does not say why cheaper moves and butterflies are enough; I only saw the mechanism on the later tape-primitive pages.

reason: Answered. I am fairly confident of the theorem statement, the machine model, the refuted conjecture (Sikited) and the overall five-step plan, since these are stated directly on the nut, kaf and siz pages. I am less sure of the exponent arithmetic and of the imported bounds (the cited estimates, the established multiplier, the rank counts), which I accepted without checking. I opened 12 of the 15 permitted pages: nut, kaf, siz, tiz, rut, bog, roz, mov, vor, kur, tab and fef.
